issue.title: Enable camera has big impact on networking
issue.body:
I test with esp32s3 on v5.2.2-163-gf81b598d10.

My device is running as an AP and I notice init camera has large impact on networking.

e.g.
Without camera init:
$ ping 192.168.10.1
PING 192.168.10.1 (192.168.10.1) 56(84) bytes of data.

After camera init:
$ ping 192.168.10.1

From 192.168.10.2 icmp_seq=40 Destination Host Unreachable

I'm wondering if this is some kind of bug in esp_camera?

I also found the cam_task is running with a very high priority (23, which is the same as wifi task priority).
The priority is not configurable, so I'm wondering if it is really necessary to run cam_task with such high priority? (Is it a good idea to make cam_task priority configurable?)

@me-no-dev 

For the "Enable camera has big impact on networking" issue,
I have confirmed this issue is realted to .xclk_freq_hz setting. ( interference issue?)
This is true for both esp32 and esp32s3.

Below symptom is exactly I observed:
https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/issues/5834
https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32/issues/5834#issuecomment-1883068251

Is there any guideline to avoid such issue?
a. from s/w, any guideline to set a good .xclk_freq_hz setting.
   currently, I did try-and-error to see the impact of different settings.
b. from h/w, is there any guideline to avoid such issue?
   e.g. https://www.reddit.com/r/esp32/comments/r9g5jc/fixing_ymmv_the_poor_frame_rate_on_the_esp32cam/

I found a similar issue on esp32-cam and I can repro with the 4 units I have, I believe this is caused by crosstalk because:

- lowering the camera clock freq reduces the problem 
- if you put your finger in certain places (causing a ground plane that shields the antenna/camera from crosstalk) the problem goes away.

 The solution was to use an external antenna, now all modules work consistently fine. 

I am surprised maintainers haven't noticed this issue given we have records of so many cases, moreover they keep giving random advice making people waste time. 

This is overall a flaky product and that is why espressif chips cost $5, what you save in one hand you lose it with a buggy platform(1600 open bugs) and unreliable support, add to that the issues some boards have (like the esp32-cam) . 

Pay a bit more and get raspberry pi stuff, no more headaches.

> I am surprised maintainers haven't noticed this issue given we have records of so many cases

We don't have a record of so many cases. AMF when I test camera, I always test it with WiFi and WebServer running and have not noticed any issues ever. S3 works the best from them all, but all 3 work fine on my end. It is very much possible that such things get influenced by other changes in IDF through time and I just did not use the particular version... If the hardware misbehaves because of crosstalk, that would need to be really proven in order to even go through the process of changing the hardware (chip internals).

> the issues some boards have (like the esp32-cam)

This is by far the works product that have ever been released with ESP32 on-board. Custom module (not made by us), bad design and routing, causing countless issues.

I can also add the fact that OmniVision have all of the supported sensors EOL and do no longer produce sensors that can work with the ESP32's parallel bus. All new sensors need MIPI. That all causes lots of bad sensors to be sold out in the wild with zero chance of support from the manufacturer. We can't even get the full registers definitions anymore

> We don't have a record of so many cases. AMF when I test camera, I always test it with WiFi and WebServer running and have not noticed any issues ever. S3 works the best from them all, but all 3 work fine on my end. 

The issue of "slow frame rate on esp32-cam devices" is pretty much ubiquitous. 

>It is very much possible that such things get influenced by other changes in IDF through time and I 
>just did not use the particular version... 

I think this issue has lasted for looong time so this discards a possible IDF issue.

>If the hardware misbehaves because of crosstalk, that would need to be really proven 
>in order to even go through the process of changing the hardware (chip internals).

I meant the boards, not the chips.

> This is by far the works product that have ever been released with ESP32 on-board. 
> Custom module (not made by us), bad design and routing, causing countless issues.

You should have spoken up and call-out bad buggy boards that don't follow your best practices. Otherwise you end up with hundreds of fustrated customers, who knows how many sales you have lost.

Another way to deal with this is by setting up a certification system where Espressif gives a seal of approval to HW boards that meet all the good practices and work as promised. (this is a common practice done by many HW companies)

> The issue of "slow frame rate on esp32-cam devices" is pretty much ubiquitous.

comments.body: This is a known behaviour when power supply is to weak and/or cooling of the ESP32 is not good enough
A lot of people including me are having this problem. It's a hardware issue. Good power makes no difference. Cooling shouldn't be an issue.
@raduprv  How should software solve a hardware issue?
No idea how it could solve it in this case, since no one seems to know what the hardware issue is. Some hardware issues can be fixed in software, some not.

I also have this problem with TTGO T-Camera Plus.

It also shows signs of temperature dependence (If I set camera resolution low and cool the board almost all problems go away) and I get good results when switching from station to AP. It’s worth mentioning that I had to disable WiFi persistence (#2025) for AP to work.

I tried with esp-idf iperf example and had bad performance (1 to 5mbit) with station mode. AP had good speeds (15 to 30mbit).

I have a m5stack timer camera, and the wifi works perfectly (not so the USB drivers for the pc though).
My room temperature is constant, around 21-25c, and the board's wifi doesn't work properly even right after I start it.

Also there seems to be some correlation (not sure) between the performance and the temperature of the board at the startup. Could be some calibration problem (I think with persistence disabled, ESP32 does full calibration at startup)

@raduprv yes I usually have bad performance when I start the board cool, but in my tests I sometimes had better performance after cooling when board is hot but just marginal.

I’m going to continue testing and check if there is really good evidence for this.

Some people reported (and I can confirm with the esp32 cam board) that when you stream video with the default test program, if you hold your fingers on certain parts of the board (towards the antenna) it gets much better.
Then I will test an external antenna soon. Can you post link of the “finger method”? :)

https://www.reddit.com/r/esp32/comments/c4iy1j/aithinker_esp32_cam_slow_video_stream_try/
https://forum.sparkfun.com/viewtopic.php?t=46563

Someone reported somewhere else that they still have wifi issues even with an external antenna, but if you are willing to try that, please let me know if it works. Don't forget to reposition the zero ohm resistor to the correct position.
Thanks I will.

I'm currently testing with an external antenna, and I have great results.

I get 50 fps on lower resolutions (with xclk set to 10mhz), 25 fps on SVGA and 6 fps on UXGA without any jitter!

There is one issue that when I move the antenna cable over some components on the board, it seems to revert back to bad performance (tests with iperf show 1 to 3mbit maximum data rate) which is very similar to the on-board antenna.

With this in mind, I assume there is either some unexpected interference problem within hardware, or they just didn't properly tune the on-board antenna when designing the boards, at least in my case.

That's good to know. I don't think the antenna design is a problem, because not everyone is having this issue.

Can you test a ftp program to upload images to a ftp server, by any chance?
If not, can you try to NOT put the board in AP mode, and try the station mode?

These results were in station mode.

I had good results with AP and on-board antenna but I suspect that was because board and the computer were near each other. Right now the distance between board and router is about 2 meters with a wall in-between (signal strength reported by the board range from -52 to -44dbm, signal strength report from router range from -62 to -57dbm) .

I suspect ftp results would be similar to my iperf speed tests, which was 15mbit average.

Then it might be a different problem. Mine doesn't work properly even if it's at ~1 meter from the router, direct line of sight.
The m5stack ones works fine though.
The signal reported by the esp32 cam is ~-52db and on the m5stack timer cam it's around -36 db. Even so, -52 db is pretty strong.

That reminds me I also moved the board near the router and still had this problem. I'm inclined to agree with you that it's not directly related to just antenna.

But there were only two factors that changed between my tests: 
* Repositioning the antenna resistor and connecting external antenna
* Other tests were two weeks ago and there were updates

My soldering iron broke so I can't change back to on-board antenna anytime soon, but it would be good if you could test external antenna. Just disconnecting the antenna makes it bad again.

all your guys hard work help me come up with a simple solution.  I had some aluminium foil tape.  Just stuck about 4 layers ontop of the circuit board antenna and its solved.  On my second module I just hot glued on thin piece of the antistatic bag it came in.  Fixed.

Bit stale, but I had issues with one board that seems to have a wide range of issue however in the run of it, the external antenna near the CPU case causes issues.

The FB buffer I set to 3. (Most sketch are 2)

issue.title: ESP32-S3: XCLK is never stopped (CAMERA_DISABLE_OUT_CLOCK is empty), streaming sensor degrades Wi-Fi even after esp_camera_deinit()
issue.body:
### Checklist

- [x] Checked the issue tracker for similar issues to ensure this is not a duplicate
- [x] Read the documentation to confirm the issue is not addressed there and your configuration is set correctly
- [x] Tested with the latest version to ensure the issue hasn't been fixed

### How often does this bug occurs?

always

### Expected behavior

Wi-Fi performance should not collapse while the camera is initialised, or at least should
return to normal after esp_camera_deinit(): XCLK should be stopped on deinit, as it is on
ESP32/ESP32-S2 via CAMERA_DISABLE_OUT_CLOCK().

### Actual behavior (suspected bug)

As soon as `esp_camera_init()` is called, Wi-Fi becomes nearly unusable (packet loss, ~0.5 s
average RTT, MQTT uploads at ~5 KB/s with keepalive timeouts), although RSSI is good
(-35 to -55 dBm). This is the same on two different APs (an ISP router and an iPhone hotspot).
The degradation **persists after `esp_camera_deinit()`**.

`esp_ping` to the gateway from the ESP, 100 pings, within a single Wi-Fi association:

| Phase | Received | RTT avg / max |
|---|---|---|
| Wi-Fi only, camera not initialised | 100/100 | 2 / 13 ms |
| `esp_camera_init()` (UXGA, streaming) | 70–86/100 | 380–460 / 1600 ms |
| after `esp_camera_deinit()` | 45–72/100 | 190–370 / 1560 ms |
| after detaching GPIO15 from `CAM_CLK_IDX` | **100/100** | **9 / 105 ms** |

On ESP32-S3, XCLK is generated by LCD_CAM and routed with
`gpio_matrix_out(pin_xclk, CAM_CLK_IDX, ...)`, but in `driver/esp_camera.c`:

    #if CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32S3 // LCD_CAM module of ESP32-S3 will generate xclk
    #define CAMERA_ENABLE_OUT_CLOCK(v)
    #define CAMERA_DISABLE_OUT_CLOCK()

and `ll_cam_deinit()` only stops/resets the CAM RX side. As a result, XCLK keeps running after
deinit, the sensor keeps streaming on the DVP bus, and the interference continues. The
"init, capture, deinit" workaround from #60 therefore does not work on S3.

Changes with no significant effect: QVGA instead of UXGA, XCLK 10 MHz, OV2640 output drive 1x
(COM2), camera task and ISR on core 1, AMPDU off, TX power 13 dBm, moving the camera module
away from the antenna.

### Error logs or terminal output

```shell
There is no crash or error code: the symptom is network degradation. Excerpts from the serial
console (application log messages translated from French; timestamps and values unchanged).

--- Run 1: same Wi-Fi association, esp_ping to gateway, 100 pings / 200 ms ---
I (7508) wifi:security: WPA2-PSK, phy: bgn, rssi: -57, cipher(pairwise:0x3, group:0x3), pmf:1
W (8568) main: TEST E1: Wi-Fi only
W (28578) diag_ping: RESULT: 100/100 received, rtt min/avg/max = 1/17/57 ms
I (28599) camera: Detected OV2640 camera
W (28771) main: TEST E2: camera UXGA active (ESP_OK)
W (121893) diag_ping: RESULT: 70/100 received, rtt min/avg/max = 1/459/1637 ms
W (121893) main: TEST F: XCLK really stopped (GPIO15 detached from LCD_CAM)
W (142396) diag_ping: RESULT: 100/100 received, rtt min/avg/max = 1/9/105 ms

--- Run 2: same sequence, but esp_camera_deinit() instead of detaching GPIO15 ---
W (90886) main: TEST E3: camera deinitialized
W (209966) diag_ping: RESULT: 45/100 received, rtt min/avg/max = 1/189/1563 ms

--- Application impact (MQTT upload of a UXGA JPEG), camera streaming ---
I (45936) mqtt_ha: Photo published: 92 KB in 17608 ms
E (47578) mqtt_client: No PING_RESP, disconnected

--- Same application with XCLK gated between captures (workaround) ---
I (14995) mqtt_ha: Photo published: 217 KB in 323 ms
```

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

1. ESP32-S3 board with an OV2640 on a DVP ribbon (here: Freenove ESP32-S3 WROOM CAM N8R8, 75 mm ribbon),
   XCLK 20 MHz on GPIO15, JPEG UXGA, fb_count 2 in PSRAM, CAMERA_GRAB_LATEST.
2. Connect to Wi-Fi (STA, power save disabled), then ping the gateway with `esp_ping`
   (100 pings, 200 ms interval): 100% received, a few ms RTT.
3. Call `esp_camera_init()` and ping again: heavy loss and RTTs of 0.4–1.6 s.
4. Call `esp_camera_deinit()` and ping again: still degraded.
5. Detach the XCLK pin from LCD_CAM:
   `esp_rom_gpio_connect_out_signal(15, SIG_GPIO_OUT_IDX, false, false); gpio_set_level(15, 0);`
   and ping again: back to 100% received, ~10 ms.

### Project release version

esp32-camera 2.1.8 (also checked: master still has the empty macro), ESP-IDF v5.5.6

### System architecture

Intel/AMD 64-bit (modern PC, older Mac)

### Operating system

Linux

### Operating system version

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS

### Shell

Bash

### Additional context

Workaround: gate XCLK between captures by detaching the pin from LCD_CAM:

    #include "esp_rom_gpio.h"
    #include "soc/gpio_sig_map.h"

    static void xclk_enable(bool on)
    {
        if (on) {
            esp_rom_gpio_connect_out_signal(PIN_XCLK, CAM_CLK_IDX, false, false);
        } else {
            esp_rom_gpio_connect_out_signal(PIN_XCLK, SIG_GPIO_OUT_IDX, false, false);
            gpio_set_level(PIN_XCLK, 0);
        }
    }

To capture: enable XCLK, discard a few frames (stale or truncated buffers; ~12 frames in UXGA
if AEC needs to re-converge after a long pause), grab one frame, then disable XCLK before
sending it. Result: 0% loss and ~15 ms ping while idle, and a 217 KB JPEG uploaded over MQTT
in 0.32 s.

Suggestions:
1. Implement CAMERA_DISABLE_OUT_CLOCK() for ESP32-S3 (detach the pin and/or stop the LCD_CAM
   clock) so that esp_camera_deinit() really stops XCLK.
2. Consider a public API to pause and resume XCLK/streaming without a full deinit
   (e.g. esp_camera_set_xclk_enabled(bool)), for applications that only need occasional captures.

Possibly related: #687, #60, espressif/arduino-esp32#11846.

comments.body:
Same issue here on an M5Stack CoreS3 (ESP32-S3), esp32-camera 2.0.4, XCLK on GPIO2 at 20 MHz.

After a single capture followed by `esp_camera_deinit()`, ping RTT between the board and a host on the same LAN stayed at 40–500 ms and never recovered. With the camera never initialised, it was 10–28 ms over 30 minutes.

Workaround in the app, after every `esp_camera_deinit()`:

```c
gpio_reset_pin(XCLK_PIN);   // detach the pin from CAM_CLK_IDX
gpio_set_direction(XCLK_PIN, GPIO_MODE_OUTPUT);
gpio_set_level(XCLK_PIN, 0);
```

The next `esp_camera_init()` routes the clock back, and captures still work. After two consecutive captures with this in place, RTT stayed at 10–16 ms.

So +1 for stopping XCLK / detaching the pin in `CAMERA_DISABLE_OUT_CLOCK()` on S3.
